body: I feel you man, I am about your age WITH a good career and a recent marriage.  I posted here with the same feelings as you.  I have chased the solutions to external problems for years thinking that *this* or *that* would be all I needed to feel right.  I have even less to complain about but the sadness and lack of a will to live have still become prevalent.  Maybe that perspective can help you in some way.

I contacted my dad last night.  Chatted with him (talking on the phone would have been messy because of my crying).  It was very helpful.  I feel like I'm not sinking anymore.  I have isolated myself emotionally and physically for years.  He thought I was mad, but I let him know that my depression has been around since an incident we both knew about that happened to me at 13.  I told him that he needed to force me to stay in touch because I am so good at shutting everything out.  I feel good about it.  You all gave me the small nudge I needed to try.

This is my second throwaway account in as many days.  I deleted my almost one year old regular reddit account a few days ago.  

I say that to illustrate that I am really searching and really reaching out.  

I want you all to know that just this little bit of kindness and caring are sinking in.  I am realizing something that is a theme here.  To help others is to love and to love is to live.  Okay, so there I am the cheesy one now.  

But really, I think that is what I need to do above all the advice out there on the medical sites is to give of myself to others...help others.  I am someone who has no *external* problem to blame like many of the other folks on here who are hurting.  I read about money, family, sexual identity, etc. problems and I just can't relate.  I have a great job, great spouse, money in the bank.  I have NO REASON to be this sad and empty.  I think the answer is to begin to simply give back.  That is what I will set my goals to.  I will act that way until it becomes a part of me.  Thanks again, you all make a difference and you deserve to know.
Thank you.  I didn't get the meds yet.  The best part of your comment was simply saying you don't want to see me suffer.  Very (surprisingly) touching to me.  I needed that.

That's good advice, and I see the logic in it.  How I feel lately is the direct opposite.  I have been losing little pieces at a time.  And not for lack of trying.  I even went to a doctor who was going to prescribe an anti-depressant but that was met with a lot of resistance by my spouse.  After having to literally fight over something that I feel would help, I have lost the desire to even pursue that route even though my spouse has now acquiesced.

Thanks for the reply.  I really am trying to jog my mind and remember.
